title: Field Sales App Cost in India
seoTitle: Field Sales App Development Cost in India (2026)
seoDescription: What a custom field sales app costs in India: beat plans, visits, orders, GPS, offline mode, CRM and Tally sync. Cost bands, timelines and cost drivers.
summary: A custom field sales app in India typically costs ₹5 lakh to ₹12 lakh for visits, orders and attendance with offline support, ₹12 lakh to ₹25 lakh with beat planning, schemes, distributor management and ERP integration, and more for large sales forces with analytics and incentives.

costBands.includes: Attendance, visits with photos and GPS, order booking, offline mode, manager dashboard
Beat plans, schemes and discounts, distributor stock, collections, Tally or ERP sync
Large teams, incentives, retail audits, advanced analytics

dataPoints.label: Must-have for India
dataPoints.value: Offline mode for poor connectivity, Hindi and regional language, low-end Android support

dataPoints.label: Biggest cost drivers
dataPoints.value: Scheme and pricing logic, offline sync, integrations

dataPoints.label: Platform
dataPoints.value: Usually React Native or Flutter, or a PWA for simpler needs

dataPoints.label: Adoption
dataPoints.value: Fast data entry and features that help salespeople, not just monitor them

body:
## What moves the price

- Offline-first design with reliable sync.
- Pricing, schemes and credit checks at order time.
- Integration with distributor and accounts systems.

See [building a field sales app for your team](/blog/building-a-field-sales-app-for-your-team) and [offline-first apps for field teams](/blog/offline-first-apps-for-field-teams-in-india).

These ranges are indicative for 2026, based on the effort such projects typically take. Your quote depends on your scope, integrations and quality requirements; a short discovery phase turns this into a firm number.

faqs.a: Most Indian field teams use Android; cross-platform frameworks make iPhone support inexpensive if needed.

faqs.q: Can GPS tracking be limited to working hours?
faqs.a: Yes, and it should be, with clear policy and consent.
